lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、大丈夫？」
lines.english: “Big Brother, are you all right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、平気……ありがとう」
lines.english: “Yes. I'm fine... Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 立っていられなくなった俺は小鳩に支えられ、近くのベンチに横たえられた。寝転がると空がよく見える。
lines.english: When my legs would no longer hold me, Kobato supported me to a nearby bench and laid me down. Flat on my back, I had a clear view of the sky.

lines.japanese: あのとき田畑の兄貴に飛びかかってからというもの、俺は教室でひとりになった。
lines.english: After the day I threw myself at Tabata's brother, I was alone in the classroom.

lines.japanese: クラスの連中は俺を遠巻きに窺いはじめ、教員たちも慎重な態度で接するようになった。
lines.english: My classmates began watching me warily from a distance, and even the teachers approached me with care.

lines.japanese: 不運なことに、ユキ姉の家から泣き声や怒鳴り声が聞こえるようになったのもあの頃だった。激情を剥き出しにした大人の罵り合いは、子供視点だと怪獣や幽霊なんかよりよっぽど恐い。
lines.english: By cruel chance, that was also when crying and shouting began to carry from Yuki’s place. To a child, adults hurling naked rage at each other were far more frightening than monsters or ghosts.

lines.japanese: いよいよ俺は家以外での話相手がいなくなった。
lines.english: At last, there was no one outside my home I could talk to.

lines.japanese: 「ひでえ少年時代だったなあ」
lines.english: “Hell of a childhood, wasn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ……」
lines.english: “I see...”

lines.japanese: 「知ってるくせに。いいよ、ちょっとずつ思いだしてきた」
lines.english: “You already know. It's all right. It's coming back to me, little by little.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか、あの騒動が決定的になったんだったな」
lines.english: “Right. That incident was what sealed it.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか、あれからだ……あれからドッジボールにも入れてもらえなくなったし、帰りもモリカワに誘ってもらえなくなったし、ウイクエごっこにも呼ばれなくなっちゃった」
lines.english: “Right. That was when it started... After that they wouldn't let me into dodgeball, nobody invited me to stop by Morikawa on the way home, and they quit calling me over to play *Wing Quest*.”

lines.japanese: 「一応いつ呼ばれてもいいように、ウイクエとウイクエごっこの練習だけは欠かさなかったんだけどなあ。でもいっくら待っても誘いが来ないんだもん。そりゃ勝手に一人四役とかやるしかねーっつうの」
lines.english: “I still practiced both *Wing Quest* and our pretend version, just in case they ever invited me again. But I waited and waited and nobody did. What else was I supposed to do but play all four parts by myself?”

lines.japanese: 「ちぇーっ、みんな俺のこと恐がっちゃってさ。ひでーよ、タッチンも川嶋もぜんぜん喋ってくんないし。田畑兄弟でさえ俺には近付かないとか、どんだけだよ」
lines.english: “Tch. Everybody got scared of me. It sucked. Tacchin and Kawashima wouldn't say a word to me, and even the Tabata brothers kept their distance. I mean, how bad is that?”

lines.japanese: 「なんか親から羽田君と遊んじゃ駄目って言われてるやつもいたし。女子なんか、川嶋の妹とか、そうそうあのブス、あいつ俺と目ぇ合っただけで泣きだしてんの。失礼だよなー、相当傷付いたぞアレ」
lines.english: “Some kids even had parents telling them not to play with Haneda. And the girls—Kawashima's little sister, remember? That ugly girl? She burst into tears just because our eyes met. Rude, right? That one hurt.”

lines.japanese: 「でもあれから私、誰にもいじめられなくなったんだよ」
lines.english: “But after that, nobody ever bullied me again.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……お兄ちゃんが私を守ってくれた」
lines.english: “Yeah... You protected me, big brother.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか。うん」
lines.english: “I see. Yes.”

lines.japanese: でも、ごめんな。
lines.english: But I'm sorry.

lines.japanese: その代わり、友達できなくなっちゃったよね。
lines.english: And the price was that you couldn't make any friends, could you?

lines.japanese: あのころ小鳩は俺に気を遣って、自分には友達がたくさんいる風を主張していた。幼い俺は疑うことを知らなかったから、あんな見えすいた嘘にころっと騙されていた。
lines.english: Back then, Kobato tried to spare my feelings by insisting she had heaps of friends. I was too young even to know how to doubt her, so that transparent lie fooled me completely.

lines.japanese: だって小鳩、たまに電話持ってぺちゃくちゃ喋ってたじゃないか。あれは誰と話してたんだよ。
lines.english: But Kobato, you used to chatter away on the telephone for ages. Who on earth were you talking to?

lines.japanese: まだ言葉もたどたどしい彼女がそうして長電話のふりを始めると、よく祖母は泣きそうな顔をしていた。俺はてっきり電話代の心配をしているのだと思っていた。
lines.english: Whenever that little girl, still stumbling over her words, launched into another pretend phone call, Grandma would look ready to cry. I assumed she was worried about the phone bill.

lines.japanese: 誰か教えてくれれば良かったのに。知ってたら妹の誕生日パーティーなんて企画は立てなかった。
lines.english: If only someone had told me. If I’d known, I would never have planned a birthday party for my little sister.

lines.japanese: あれは子供なりに結構な金をかけたんだ。お菓子やらケーキやらパーティーグッズやら。クリスマス会も兼ねてるから、参加賞のプレゼントとして駄菓子屋でおもちゃもいっぱい調達した。
lines.english: By a child's standards, I sank serious money into it: candy, cake, party decorations. It was doubling as a Christmas party, so I bought a mountain of little toys from the candy shop as prizes for everyone who came.

lines.japanese: 会場──つうか団地の一室、つうか俺の家、つうか四畳半の子供部屋──を、ガキ特有の足し算思考と図工の才を発揮してでたらめに飾りつけた。
lines.english: I decorated the venue—meaning one room in the housing complex, meaning our apartment, meaning our tiny bedroom—with a child's more-is-more aesthetic and the full force of my artistic gifts.

lines.japanese: チラシはアナログで３０枚作った。材料は片面印刷の折り込み広告、クレヨン、資料のポスター、瑞々しい感性、図工の才、妹を祝ってあげたいと思う気持ち、１０分×３０枚分の制作時間。
lines.english: I made thirty flyers by hand. Materials: the blank sides of newspaper inserts, crayons, a poster for reference, fresh young sensibility, artistic genius, the desire to celebrate my sister, and ten minutes of work on every single one.

lines.japanese: 俺のクレヨン使いには定評があって、破局前のケン兄たちからは図工の王子様と称えられていた。だからチラシの出来にはわりと自信があったんだけど、近所で配っても四枚しか受けとってもらえなかった。
lines.english: My crayon work enjoyed considerable acclaim. Before their breakup, Ken and Yuki had hailed me as the Prince of Arts and Crafts. So I was fairly confident in those flyers, but only four people in the neighborhood would even take one.

lines.japanese: ちなみに四枚のうち一枚は小鳩、あとの三枚は最寄りのごみ箱へと行きわたった。だからパーティーの出席者は俺と小鳩だけだった。それなら最初からバアちゃんたちに外出してもらわなければ良かった。
lines.english: For the record, Kobato took one. The other three found their way to the nearest trash can. So the party guests were Kobato and me. In that case, I should never have asked Grandma and the others to clear out for us.

lines.japanese: 大量に余ってしまった菓子やケーキを、小鳩は懸命に頬張りながら、ぜんぶ二人占めできて嬉しいねと苦しそうに笑っていた。
lines.english: We were left with mountains of candy and cake. Kobato valiantly stuffed her cheeks and smiled through the pain, saying how wonderful it was that we got it all to ourselves.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとな、ポッポ」
lines.english: “Thank you, Poppo.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 俺はあのころの妹に心から感謝した。
lines.english: With all my heart, I thanked the little sister she had been then.

lines.japanese: 彼女はいま、俺に守ってもらったと言っていた。でも──
lines.english: She had just said I protected her. But—

lines.japanese: 「──俺だって小鳩がいてくれたから救われたんだ」
lines.english: “—Kobato, you saved me too.”

lines.japanese: 「俺の味方は小鳩だけだったから」
lines.english: “Because you were the only one on my side.”

lines.japanese: お互いしか縋るものがなかった。
lines.english: We had no one to cling to but each other.

lines.japanese: お互いしか頼ってくれるものがいなかった。
lines.english: And neither of us had anyone else who needed us.

lines.japanese: だから相手を救うことで自分が救われていた俺たち。
lines.english: We had saved ourselves by saving each other.

lines.japanese: 「行こう」
lines.english: “Let's go.”
“O-okay...”

lines.japanese: 俺は立ちあがった。恐くて仕方なかったけれど、小鳩の優しさをすべて思いだすために。
lines.english: I stood. I was terrified, but I had to remember every kindness Kobato had ever shown me.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、懐かしいな……」
lines.english: “Ahh. This takes me back...”

lines.japanese: あのころ住んでいた公団住宅。
lines.english: The public housing complex where we had lived.

lines.japanese: 巨大団地群のほとりに立って、俺はまだうじうじと逡巡していた。
lines.english: Standing at the edge of that enormous housing estate, I still lingered in miserable indecision.

lines.japanese: 甦ったばかりの記憶の片鱗が、忌まわしい過去の影が、頭の裏側に焼きついて離れないからだ。
lines.english: The fragments of memory that had just surfaced—the shadows of that hateful past—stayed burned into the back of my mind.

lines.japanese: あのあと田畑の兄貴はすぐさま病院へ運ばれたという。幸い大事には至らなかった。
lines.english: Tabata's brother, I learned, was rushed straight to the hospital. Fortunately, his injuries were not serious.

lines.japanese: 俺はもうひとりの俺がしでかしたことをすっぽり忘れている状態で我に返った。
lines.english: I came back to myself with no memory at all of what my other self had done.

lines.japanese: だから逃げだしたのはそのときじゃない。居場所をなくして世界に背を向けたのは、まだ先だ。
lines.english: So that was not when I ran. The day I lost my place in the world and turned my back on it was still to come.

lines.japanese: そこに……なにかがあるんだ。思いださなくてはいけないなにか。
lines.english: There was... something there. Something I had to remember.

lines.japanese: しかし忘れていたいなにか。
lines.english: Something I wanted to keep forgotten.

lines.japanese: あたかも本能のように俺は知っていた。それを知るのは恐いことだと。自我の崩壊さえ危ぶまれる、とてもとても恐ろしいことだと。
lines.english: I knew it almost by instinct: whatever it was, to know it would be terrifying—so terrifying it might shatter the self itself.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん」
lines.english: “Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: 「ここから先は……しんどそうだ」
lines.english: “From here on... this is going to hurt.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩と目を合わせられない。すべての風景から目を逸らしたくなる。
lines.english: I couldn't meet Kobato's eyes. I wanted to look away from every part of the landscape.

lines.japanese: 不安は恐怖へ、恐怖は悪心へ。心拍数が跳ねあがって、呼吸が苦しくなってきた。世界が……世界が平和で……ええと、なんだっけ。なんでもいいや。
lines.english: Anxiety became fear; fear became nausea. My pulse leaped and every breath grew harder. The world... May the world be... uh, what was it? Who cares.

lines.japanese: なんでもいい。どうでもいい。なあ、逃げちゃっていいんじゃないか、このまま。
lines.english: Who cares. None of it matters. Hey—why don't I just run? Right now.

lines.japanese: そうだよ俺、根性ないもん。耐えられるわけないよ。ほんと勘弁してください。
lines.english: That's right. I've got no backbone. There's no way I can take this. Please. Just let me off.

lines.japanese: めまい。誰かの声。膝が折れる。回れ右して逃げかえれと心のどこかが言っている。
lines.english: Vertigo. Someone's voice. My knees gave way. Somewhere inside, something told me to turn around and run home.

lines.japanese: ここではないどこかへ。柳木原でも、グレタガルドでも、なんだったら奈落でもいい。どうせコンドルさんが待ってる。あいつは俺の潜在意識みたいなものだから。
lines.english: Anywhere but here. Yanagihara, Gretagard, even the Abyss for all I cared. Mr. Condor would be waiting there anyway. He was practically my subconscious.

lines.japanese: 俺を見あげた小鳩の手に、わずかな力が加わる。
lines.english: Kobato looked up at me, and her hand tightened faintly.

lines.japanese: 俺の迷いや惑いは外に漏れていたんだろう。もの言わぬ眼差しが、もう逃げるなと告げているようだ。逃げたらまた逆戻り、同じことの繰り返しだ。
lines.english: My hesitation and panic must have shown. Her silent gaze seemed to say: don't run again. If I ran, I would only go back to the beginning and live it all over.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、私」
lines.english: “Big Brother, I...”

lines.japanese: しかし彼女は俺を咎めるでも追いたてるでもなく──
lines.english: But she neither blamed me nor urged me on—

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんといっしょにいたい」
lines.english: “I want to stay with you, Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: ──ただ子供のように純粋な願いを伝えるだけだった。
lines.english: —she only gave voice to a wish as pure as a child's.

lines.japanese: 裏返せばそれは、俺の逃げ道をふさぐ言葉だ。いまの俺に取っては、前へ進んでほしいと懇願されたに等しい。
lines.english: Yet those words also sealed off my escape. In that moment, they amounted to a plea for me to keep going.

lines.japanese: だけど彼女にそんな意図や打算はなかったんだろう。だって小鳩はいつもそうだったから。
lines.english: But she probably had no such intention or calculation. Kobato had always been like that.

lines.japanese: 子供のように純粋な願い。遠慮のない、だけど押しつけがましくもない、兄妹同然に一緒だったふたりだからぶつけ合える、素のままの気持ち。
lines.english: A child’s pure wish, unreserved but never demanding—the kind of simple feeling two people raised almost as brother and sister could say aloud to each other.

lines.japanese: 大人のように慎みぶかく生きることを強いられてきた彼女は、俺の前でだけありのままの子供に戻る。
lines.english: She had been forced to live with an adult's reserve. Only with me could she return to the child she truly was.

lines.japanese: だから妹の可愛らしい我がままには応えてやりたいと、いつも俺はそう思っていた。
lines.english: That was why I had always wanted to indulge my little sister's adorable selfishness.

lines.japanese: 無邪気でまっすぐで他人の顔色を窺わない、当り前の子供らしく居させてやりたかったんだ。
lines.english: I had wanted to let her be an ordinary child: innocent, forthright, never checking other people's faces before she spoke.

lines.japanese: そうだ。
lines.english: That's right.

lines.japanese: あの頃の俺は、いつもそう思っていたんだ。
lines.english: That was what I had always thought back then.

lines.japanese: 「おにいちゃん、おかしちょうだい」
lines.english: “Big Brother, can I have a snack?”

lines.japanese: 妹はやたら俺にせびる子供だった。
lines.english: My little sister had been a child forever begging things from me.

lines.japanese: とくに言葉を覚えはじめてからは、しょっちゅう両手を差しだしてきた。
lines.english: Especially once she began to learn words, she was forever holding out both hands.

lines.japanese: 「もー、ポッポはー食いしんぼさんなんだからー。兄ちゃんさっきいっぱいあげたでしょー？　あともうペロリチョコしかのこってないのよー」
lines.english: “Oh, Poppo, what a greedy little thing you are. I gave you loads already, remember? I’ve only got one little chocolate left.”

lines.japanese: 「わーい、チョコレート大すき！」
lines.english: “Hooray! I love chocolate!”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、こんな小っこいの、一コだけでよろこんじった。ポッポはなんでもよろこんじゃうのねー」
lines.english: “Ahaha, look at you! One teeny piece and you're over the moon. Anything makes Poppo happy, doesn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「うんありがとー、おにいちゃん！」
lines.english: “Yes! Thanks, Big Brother!”

lines.japanese: 可愛い妹。彼女を愛すことに疑問なんてなかった。
lines.english: My darling little sister. Loving her had never been a question.

lines.japanese: 新しい家族。彼女を守りたいと思う気持ちに、理由付けする必要なんてなかった。
lines.english: My new family. I had needed no reason for wanting to protect her.

lines.japanese: お兄ちゃんなんだから面倒みなさいって、いつもずっと言われてた。けど、もし大人たちから強制されなかったとしても、きっと俺は同じように小鳩の世話をしただろう──
lines.english: They were always telling me that I was the big brother, so I had to look after her. But even if the adults had never made me, I was sure I would have cared for Kobato just the same—

lines.japanese: ──彼女に俺しかいなかったのと同様、俺にだって彼女しかいなかったんだから。
lines.english: —because just as I was all she had, she was all I had.

lines.japanese: 「……うん。もう大丈夫」
lines.english: “...Yes. I'm all right now.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 追憶から帰ってきたとき、俺は小鳩の手を握って一点を見据えていた。五街区の一棟、かつての住まい。
lines.english: When I surfaced from the memory, I was clutching Kobato's hand and staring at a single point: one building in Block Five, our former home.

lines.japanese: いままた迷いは断ちきった。
lines.english: Once again, I had cut through my hesitation.

lines.japanese: ここからはおそらくこの繰り返しになるだろう。立ちあがり、進み、惑い、止まり、後ずさり、膝をつく。
lines.english: From here on, it would probably be this same cycle: rise, advance, falter, stop, retreat, fall to my knees.

lines.japanese: けれど俺は、そのたび最愛の家族を想って立ちあがろう。
lines.english: But each time, I would think of my dearest family and stand again.

lines.japanese: 「ここまで来たんだ、もう逃げない。もう夢テレビは点けない」
lines.english: “I've come this far. I won't run again. I won't turn on the dream TV again.”
“Y-yes...”

lines.japanese: 歩みは遅いかもしれない。でもちょっとずつ前へ進もう。
lines.english: My steps might be slow, but I would move forward little by little.

lines.japanese: 彼女が共にいるかぎり。
lines.english: So long as she was with me.

lines.japanese: 「さあ、かかって来やがれだ──」
lines.english: “All right, then. Come and get me—”

lines.japanese: 俺はどすんと腰を落とし、芝の上にあぐらをかいた。キャッチボールに興じていた小学生たちが、気を遣ってすこし距離を離してくれる。
lines.english: I dropped heavily onto the grass and sat cross-legged. The grade-school boys playing catch nearby tactfully put a little more distance between us.

lines.japanese: 「──ぜんぶ思いだしてやる」
lines.english: “—I'll remember everything.”

lines.japanese: 睨みすえた視線の先はかつてのふるさと。
lines.english: I stared hard at the place that had once been home.

lines.japanese: 記憶の扉はここから開こう。
lines.english: Here was where I would open the door to memory.

lines.japanese: 母はときどき俺を誰かと間違えていた。
lines.english: Sometimes Mother mistook me for someone else.

lines.japanese: “ごめんね鷹志。本当にごめんね”
lines.english: “I'm sorry, Takashi. I'm so terribly sorry.”

lines.japanese: そして最後はいつも俺に謝った。
lines.english: In the end, she always apologized to me.

lines.japanese: 俺はやめてほしいと思っていたけど、母を嫌いになったことは一度もなかった。
lines.english: I wanted her to stop, but I never once hated my mother.

lines.japanese: 「お母さんは仕事から帰ってきても、俺に疲れた顔なんて見せなかった。優しくて頑張り屋の、すごくいいひとだった」
lines.english: “Even after she came home from work, Mom never let me see how tired she was. She was kind and hardworking. A truly good person.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、そんなお母さんを周りのみんなが悪く言うのが、ずっと不思議だったんだ」
lines.english: “But everyone around us spoke badly of her. I could never understand why.”

lines.japanese: 俺には父親がいないってことを理解したのは、母親が俺を連れて単身実家──この町──に戻ったころ。物心ついてすぐだった。
lines.english: I understood that I had no father around the time Mother took me back alone to her family home in this town. I had only just become old enough to know anything at all.

lines.japanese: 当時は近所の兄ちゃんたちが投げかけてくる心ない言葉の意味も、半分ぐらいはよく分からなかった。おまえの父ちゃんがどうとか、母ちゃんがこうとか。
lines.english: Back then, I understood perhaps half of the cruel things the older neighborhood boys threw at me—something about my father, something about my mother.

lines.japanese: 俺はそんなこと気にしてなかったのに、母親はしきりに謝ってた。よく分からないから、いいよいいよっていつも適当に手を振ってた。
lines.english: I didn't care, yet Mother apologized constantly. I didn't understand, so I always waved it away and said it was fine.

lines.japanese: 「お母さんはいつも誰かに謝ってた気がする。味方がいなかった自分を迎えてくれたバアちゃんにも、叔父さんにも叔母さんにも……それから近所のひとにも、仕事場のひとにも。あと、俺にも」
lines.english: “I feel as though Mom was always apologizing to someone. To Grandma, who took her in when she had no one else; to my uncle and aunt... to the neighbors, the people at work. And to me.”

lines.japanese: そのうち叔父さんと叔母さんの間に娘が生まれた。
lines.english: In time, my uncle and aunt had a daughter.

lines.japanese: 俺は同じ家にいる年下の女の子だから、わりと長いこと本気で妹だと思ってた。大人たちも当たり前のようにそうみなしていたし。
lines.english: She was a younger girl living under the same roof, so for quite a long time I honestly believed she was my sister. The adults treated us as brother and sister too, as though it went without saying.

lines.japanese: 「お母さんにいつも言われてたよ。鷹志はお兄ちゃんなんだから、妹のポッポを守らなきゃいけないのよって。うんとかわいがってあげなさいって」
lines.english: “Mom told me all the time: ‘Takashi, you're the big brother. You have to protect your little sister Poppo. You be very, very good to her.’”

lines.japanese: 「うん、お兄ちゃんのお母さん優しかった」
lines.english: “Yes. Your mother was kind.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね……最初のうちは」
lines.english: “She was... at first.”

lines.japanese: 母が変わったのは、妹が言葉を覚えはじめてからだった。
lines.english: Mother changed when my sister began learning to speak.

lines.japanese: “離れなさいよ、この泥棒猫！”
lines.english: “Get away from him, you thieving little tramp!”

lines.japanese: 彼女はときどき俺を誰かと間違えたように、小鳩のこともときどき誰かと混同するようになった。
lines.english: Just as she sometimes mistook me for someone else, she began mistaking Kobato for someone too.

lines.japanese: そんなときの母はまるで別人のようだった。
lines.english: At such times, Mother became a different person.

lines.japanese: “なんで！　なんでよ！　私のことは捨てたくせに、なんでそんな女とベタベタしてんのよ！”
lines.english: “Why?! Why?! You abandoned me, so why are you all over that woman?!”

lines.japanese: 俺は身を固くしながら小鳩の前に立った。
lines.english: I stiffened and stood in front of Kobato.

lines.japanese: “やめてよ、お母さん。ポッポはわるくないよ、ポッポはなにもしてないよ”
lines.english: “Stop, Mom. Poppo didn't do anything. Poppo didn't do anything wrong.”

lines.japanese: “私のこと好きって言ってくれたのに！　あんなに何度も愛してくれたのに！”
lines.english: “You said you loved me! You made love to me so many times!”

lines.japanese: “ちがうよお母さん、ぼくお父さんじゃないよ”
lines.english: “That's wrong, Mom. I'm not Dad.”

lines.japanese: “い、いたっ……いたい、むりだよ、やめてよう”
lines.english: I-it hurts... It hurts. I can't. Stop, please.

lines.japanese: そのときの母の熱い息遣いを思いだすと、頭が割れるように痛む。
lines.english: When I remember Mother's hot breath at those times, my head feels ready to split.

lines.japanese: 母が豹変する機会は、日を追うごとに少しずつ増えていった。
lines.english: Mother's transformations came a little more often with every passing day.

lines.japanese: 俺が幼い小鳩の遊び相手をしていると、大声をあげて俺たちに飛びかかってくることもあった。
lines.english: If I played with little Kobato, Mother sometimes screamed and threw herself at us.

lines.japanese: しかし俺や小鳩がひとりずつだったり、他の第三者がいたりする場では、あの優しくて頑張り屋の大好きな母のままだった。
lines.english: Yet if Kobato or I was alone, or if anyone else was present, she remained the kind, hardworking mother I adored.

lines.japanese: 彼女がたまに恐い母になってしまうのは、悪霊だか悪魔だかの仕業だと本気で思っていた。当時、母は新興宗教に救いを求めていたが、俺の幼ない感性にはそれが特撮番組の邪教めいて見えてたんだ。
lines.english: I truly believed an evil spirit or demon was responsible whenever she turned into the frightening Mother. She was seeking salvation in a new religion then, but to my childish eyes it looked like the wicked cult in a masked-hero show.

lines.japanese: そしてこのことが知れたら、母が暗黒大教団の生贄にされてしまうと考えていたので、決して他言はしなかった。
lines.english: And I believed that if anyone found out, Mother would be offered up as a sacrifice to the Grand Church of Darkness. So I never told another soul.

lines.japanese: “鷹志は小鳩が大好きなのね。ふふふ、兄妹ずーっと仲良くするのよ”
lines.english: “Takashi loves Kobato, doesn't he? Hee-hee. You two stay close forever.”

lines.japanese: “ふざけんな！　ふざけんな！　ふざけんな！　私のヨシキに近づくな、この雌豚ああぁぁぁ！！”
lines.english: “Don't fuck with me! Don't fuck with me! Don't fuck with me! Stay away from my Yoshiki, you filthy sow!”

lines.japanese: “ただいまぁー。伯母さん、小鳩の好きなチョコレートケーキ買ってきたの。三人で食べよう？”
lines.english: “I'm home! Auntie, I bought Kobato's favorite chocolate cake. Let's all eat it together.”

lines.japanese: “どうして私よりこの女を選ぶのおおおッ！　ねえお願い、もう一度、お願いだから私のこと愛してよぉ……”
lines.english: “Why are you choosing this woman over me?! Please—one more time. Please, love me again...”

lines.japanese: 普段の母は大好きだったけれど、悪霊に憑かれたときの母に接するときはいつも、悲しいとも寂しいとも違う名状しがたい気持ちになった。
lines.english: I loved Mother as she ordinarily was. But whenever the evil spirit possessed her, I felt something unlike sadness or loneliness, something beyond all naming.

lines.japanese: それから母は何度も仕事を変えた。周囲のひとに頭を下げる回数も増えていった。
lines.english: After that, Mother changed jobs again and again. She found herself bowing apologies to the people around her more and more.

lines.japanese: 家では布団から出てこられない時間が増えたが、しかし心配事が多くてどうしても眠れないとかで、しばしば向精神薬に頼っていた。
lines.english: At home, she spent longer and longer unable to get out of bed. Yet she said she had too many worries to sleep at all, and often turned to psychiatric medication.

lines.japanese: 「お母さんは豹変してしまう自分が許せなかったんだと思う。本当は小鳩のことが大好きだったから」
lines.english: “I think Mom couldn't forgive the person she became. Because the truth was, she loved Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんのことも大好きだった。だから私、お兄ちゃんのお母さんのことは嫌いじゃなかった」
lines.english: “She loved you too. That's why I never hated your mother.”

lines.japanese: 「……ありがとう」
lines.english: “...Thank you.”

lines.japanese: しかし母はどんどん壊れていった。
lines.english: But Mother went on breaking, piece by piece.

lines.japanese: 寝酒が高じて、アルコールの摂取量が飛躍的に増えていった。
lines.english: Her nightcaps became a habit, and the amount of alcohol she consumed soared.

lines.japanese: 仕事も勤まらず、しょっちゅう手酌で日本酒を煽りながら、同じライブビデオばかり延々と繰りかえし観ていた。
lines.english: Unable to hold down a job, she would sit pouring herself cup after cup of rice wine and watch the same concert video over and over.

lines.japanese: そんなとき俺は母が暴れださないよう小鳩から離れて、だけど小鳩が危ない目に合わないよう、押入れに隠れて震えながら母を見張っていた。
lines.english: At those times, I kept my distance from Kobato so Mother wouldn’t lash out. But to make sure Kobato stayed safe, I hid in the closet and watched Mother, trembling.

lines.japanese: わずかな隙間から覗く光のステージと夢のような王子たちは、息詰まる不安や恐怖をわずかながらでも和らげてくれたものだ。
lines.english: Through that narrow crack, a radiant stage and princes out of a dream would ease the suffocating fear and anxiety, if only a little.

lines.japanese: ある日、母が中身の残ったグラスを壁に叩きつけた。
lines.english: One day, Mother hurled a half-full glass against the wall.

lines.japanese: 外から押入れのふすまが開けはなたれ、俺は刹那の戦慄を覚えた。仁王立ちする彼女の背後では、永遠の王子たちがキラキラと舞いおどっていた。いつだってプリズン。
lines.english: The closet door flew open from outside, and terror took me in an instant. Behind Mother, standing with her legs planted wide, the eternal princes danced and glittered. *Always a Prison*.

lines.japanese: 次の瞬間、母の手が、俺を布団だらけの独居房から引きずりだした。
lines.english: In the next instant, Mother's hand dragged me from my solitary cell among the piled bedding.

lines.japanese: しかしそれは、石鹸と糠味噌の香りがするとても優しい力だった。
lines.english: Yet the force was very gentle, and smelled of soap and rice-bran pickles.

lines.japanese: “ごめんね、ごめんね”
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 母は俺をむちゃくちゃに抱きしめた。あの温かさは克明に思いだせる。
lines.english: Mother gathered me into a frantic embrace. I can remember that warmth in perfect detail.

lines.japanese: 彼女の体から悪霊が出ていったのだと思って、俺は安堵した。悪いのはぜんぶ悪霊のせいだから、母に謝ってもらう必要はない。俺は涙に濡れた真っ赤な目を覗きこんで、笑った。
lines.english: I thought the evil spirit had left her body, and relief washed through me. Everything bad had been the spirit's fault, so Mother had nothing to apologize for. I peered into her red, tear-drenched eyes and smiled.

lines.japanese: “なぁーんもう。おれ、ぜんぜんいかってねーからよー、そんなん気にすんなてー”
lines.english: “Aw, c'mon. I'm not mad at all, so don't you worry about it.”

lines.japanese: 悪霊が去ったと知って、小鳩も隣りの部屋からおずおずやって来た。俺と目が合うとえへへと笑った。
lines.english: When she knew the spirit was gone, Kobato crept in from the next room. Our eyes met, and she smiled shyly.

lines.japanese: 次の瞬間、俺の体は食器棚に激突していた。
lines.english: The next instant, my body struck the cupboard.

lines.japanese: “おまえらデキてんのかあああああ！”
lines.english: “Are you two screwing each other?!”

lines.japanese: 悪霊が母の体を使って絶叫した。
lines.english: The evil spirit screamed through Mother's body.

lines.japanese: 俺は恐怖と激痛でわけが分からなかったけれど、優しい方の母の言いつけどおり、妹の身をかばって体を丸めた。
lines.english: Fear and agony left me unable to understand anything. Still, just as the kind Mother had taught me, I curled my body around my little sister and shielded her.

lines.japanese: 「ダメだってー！　ポッポんこといじめたらダメでしょーう！」
lines.english: Nooo! You can't pick on Poppo!

lines.japanese: “なあああんでええええええ！”
lines.english: “Why?! Why?! Why?!”

lines.japanese: 悪霊は俺の首根を掴んだ。恐ろしいほどの力だった。俺は小鳩の体から引きはがされ、ぼろ雑巾のように投げすてられた。
lines.english: The spirit seized me by the scruff of the neck with terrifying strength. It tore me away from Kobato and flung me aside like a filthy rag.

lines.japanese: それでも小鳩を守りたくて、必死に手を伸ばした。
lines.english: Even then, I wanted to protect her. I reached out desperately.

lines.japanese: “ああ゛あああ゛あ゛あぁぁぁーッ！”
lines.english: “Aaaaaaaaaagh!”

lines.japanese: 悪霊は奇声を発しながら、俺や小鳩や食器や家具やその他いろいろを見境なく打ちまくった。
lines.english: Screeching, the spirit lashed out blindly at me, at Kobato, at the dishes and furniture—at anything and everything.

lines.japanese: “なんでっ！　なんで私と鷹志を捨てたああああ！”
lines.english: “Why?! Why did you abandon Takashi and me?!”

lines.japanese: 悪霊の凄絶な形相とおぞましい咆哮は、俺の幼い精神を凍りつけて麻痺させた。
lines.english: The spirit's ghastly face and hideous roar froze my young mind numb.

lines.japanese: だけど俺は気を失うわけにいかなかった。誰かの力を借りてでも、可愛い妹を守らねばならない。優しい母を取りかえさねばならない。忌むべき悪霊を追いはらわねばならない。
lines.english: But I could not let myself faint. I had to borrow someone's strength if that was what it took to protect my darling sister, to win back my gentle mother, to drive out that hateful spirit.

lines.japanese: 「ポッポはおれがまもったげんのー！」
lines.english: “I'm gonna protect Poppo!”

lines.japanese: そこから先は記憶があやふやだ。そのときの俺自身があやふやだったせいだろう。
lines.english: After that, my memory grew hazy. Perhaps because I myself had grown hazy then.

lines.japanese: たしか俺は、短い腕を振りあげて突撃したんだと思う。次に悪霊の尾が俺の体を吹きとばした。
lines.english: I think I raised my little arms and charged. Then the spirit's tail sent me flying.

lines.japanese: 頭をしたたかに打った俺は、身をよじってのたうった。口を開けば胃の中のものが飛びだしそうだった。
lines.english: My head struck hard. I twisted and writhed; if I opened my mouth, everything in my stomach would come spilling out.

lines.japanese: 悪霊が小鳩に迫る。俺は後頭部の痛みに眩惑されながら、激しく敵を呪った。
lines.english: The spirit closed in on Kobato. Dazzled by the pain in the back of my skull, I cursed my enemy with all my strength.

lines.japanese: なんでこんなことすんだよ……！
lines.english: Why was it doing this...?

lines.japanese: このやろう……どいつもこいつも……なんでおれン家ばっかいじめんだよ……！
lines.english: You bastard... Every one of you... Why do you always pick on my family...?

lines.japanese: どこのだれだよ！　おれたち、いじめんのは！
lines.english: Who are you?! Who's doing this to us?!

lines.japanese: 俺は俺の大事なものを傷付けようとする悪意に憤りを覚えた。
lines.english: Rage rose in me at the malice that meant to hurt the things I treasured.

lines.japanese: 誰かをやっつけてやりたいと思う気持ち。
lines.english: The desire to beat someone down.

lines.japanese: 台所でなにかが小さく光っていた。
lines.english: Something small gleamed in the kitchen.

lines.japanese: どこかで誰かが力を貸そうと誘っていた。
lines.english: Somewhere, someone invited me to borrow his strength.

lines.japanese: 小鳩は泣いていた。
lines.english: Kobato was crying.

lines.japanese: 母もたぶん泣いていた。
lines.english: Mother was probably crying too.

lines.japanese: 俺も泣きたかった。
lines.english: I wanted to cry.

lines.japanese: 俺は狂いそうだった。
lines.english: I was going mad.

lines.japanese: 俺は気を失いそうだった。
lines.english: I was losing consciousness.

lines.japanese: 俺は誰かに助けてほしかった。
lines.english: I wanted someone to save me.

lines.japanese: 俺はここから逃げてしまいたかった。
lines.english: I wanted to escape from here.

lines.japanese: だけどどうしても大事なものを守りたかった。
lines.english: But no matter what, I wanted to protect what I loved.

lines.japanese: あらゆる理不尽への怒りで目の前が血の赤に染まっていた。
lines.english: Rage at every senseless wrong stained the world before me blood-red.

lines.japanese: 台所でなにかが赤く光っていた。
lines.english: Something in the kitchen glowed red.

lines.japanese: どこかで誰かが俺に任せろと嗤っていた。
lines.english: Somewhere, someone laughed derisively and told me to leave it all to him.

lines.japanese: あんたはすっこんでりゃいいんだよ。
lines.english: You can stand back and stay out of it.

lines.japanese: 堪えなくていいんだよ。楽になっちゃえよ。
lines.english: You don't have to endure anymore. Let yourself go.

lines.japanese: もういいじゃないか。
lines.english: Come on. That's enough, isn't it?

lines.japanese: 狂っちゃおう、気楽に。
lines.english: Let's go crazy. It'll be easier.

lines.japanese: 俺は朦朧とした意識の中で、それはいい考えだなあと思った。
lines.english: In my fading haze, I thought that sounded like a great idea.

lines.japanese: <8>\「うヴぁああああァァァー！」
lines.english: “Uwaaaaaaaaaagh!”

lines.japanese: 鬱積した怨嗟が姿なき悪意に放たれる──
lines.english: All the hatred festering inside me burst toward a malice without form—

lines.japanese: ──と思ったら姿はあった。
lines.english: —or so I thought. It had a form after all.

lines.japanese: ある平和な公団住宅を騒がせたその事件ののち、くだんの児童は相応の施設へ移送された。
lines.english: Following the incident that disturbed the peace of a certain public housing complex, the child concerned was transferred to an appropriate institution.

lines.japanese: 児童の妹は、凄惨な光景を目の当たりにしたことで深刻な心的外傷を負い、なかば昏迷状態に近かったという。保護者の希望で、兄妹は同じ施設へ入所した。
lines.english: His younger sister, having witnessed the horrific scene firsthand, suffered grave psychological trauma and reportedly fell into something approaching a stupor. At their guardian's request, the siblings were admitted to the same institution.

lines.japanese: 「俺じゃないか……」
lines.english: “That was me...”

lines.japanese: 「お母さんを……のは……俺だ……」
lines.english: “Mom... The one who... was me...”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん？　違うよ」
lines.english: “Big brother? No, that’s not true.”

lines.japanese: 「あッ、あああッ、あッ！」
lines.english: “Ah! Aaaah! Ah!”

lines.japanese: 「俺だよ、俺が自分で……あっ、あぁぁぁ！」
lines.english: “It was me. I did it with my own hands... Aaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、お兄ちゃんしっかりして」
lines.english: “Big brother! Big brother, pull yourself together!”

lines.japanese: 体が揺さぶられる。小鳩が見える。俺の心配をしてくれている。
lines.english: My body shook. I could see Kobato. She was worried about me.

lines.japanese: 自分をしっかり保たなくちゃいけない。しかしそう思うほどに、溢れる涙は止まらず頬を濡らしていった。
lines.english: I had to hold myself together. Yet the harder I tried, the more the tears spilled over and soaked my cheeks.

lines.japanese: 「だから俺は逃げてたんだ……思いださないように……過去に捕まらないように……」
lines.english: “That's why I ran... So I wouldn't remember... So the past couldn't catch me...”

lines.japanese: 「ううっ……俺が、俺が大好きなお母さんを！」
lines.english: “Ugh... I—I did that to the mother I loved!”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん！」
lines.english: “Big brother!”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさいごめんなさいごめんなさいごめんなさいごめんなさあい！」
lines.english: “I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorrrrrry!”

lines.japanese: 心からの懺悔だった。
lines.english: It was repentance from the bottom of my heart.

lines.japanese: だけど赦してもらおうとは思わなかった。当たり前だ。赦してくれるひとはもういないのだから。
lines.english: But I did not expect to be forgiven. Of course I didn't. The one person who could forgive me was already gone.

lines.japanese: そうだ。俺は赦されなかったんだ。
lines.english: That was it. I had never been forgiven.

lines.japanese: だから自らを断罪した。
lines.english: So I passed judgment upon myself.

lines.japanese: 消せない十字架を背負った俺に、この素晴らしい世界からの追放を宣告した。
lines.english: Bearing a cross that could never be erased, I sentenced myself to exile from this wonderful world.

lines.japanese: 奈落行きの終身刑を科して、二度と陽の目を見るなと命じた。
lines.english: I condemned myself to life in the Abyss and ordered myself never to see daylight again.

lines.japanese: そして小鳩を守るために別の自分を残していった。
lines.english: And I left other selves behind to protect Kobato.

lines.japanese: 思いだしてしまった。
lines.english: I had remembered.

lines.japanese: 「う、ううっ……うううう……」
lines.english: “U-ugh... Uuuugh...”

lines.japanese: 「もう……もうやだ……おれ、かえる……」
lines.english: “No... No more... I wanna go home...”

lines.japanese: 「ならくかえって……夢テレビみて……やなことぜんぶ忘れるんだ……」
lines.english: “Go home to the Abyss... Watch dream TV... Forget every bad thing...”

lines.japanese: 「ぱちっ、ぶわあん……」
lines.english: “Click... whoom...”

lines.japanese: 「じぇっ、ＪＯ俺Ｒ－ＴＶ……こここちらは奈落……」
lines.english: “J-JO-ORE-R TV... Th-this is the Abyss...”

lines.japanese: 「は、羽田くん、さいってー……じゃなかった、さいこーう！」
lines.english: “H-Haneda, you're the wooorst... No, I mean the beeeest!”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん」
lines.english: “Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、はッ……な、なななに見てんだブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ、ぶぶ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウッ……」
lines.english: “Ha... hah... Wh-what are you looking at? I’ll kill you, asshole. I-I’ll kill you, asshole...”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、自分の中に逃げだしちゃダメだよ」
lines.english: “Big brother, don’t run away inside yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「うるさいっ、俺は、俺はっ……」
lines.english: “Shut up! I—I...”

lines.japanese: 「ここにいちゃいけない奴なんだよ！」
lines.english: “I'm someone who isn't supposed to be here!”

lines.japanese: 「だって……俺ほんとはここにいないんだよ……だから見ないでよ……」
lines.english: “Because... the truth is, I'm not really here... So please don't look at me...”

lines.japanese: 「あぅ、あああっ……」
lines.english: “Ah... aaaah...”

lines.japanese: 「見るなよ……俺を見るな……」
lines.english: “Don't look... Don't look at me...”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうだ、あの、お兄ちゃん、えと……牧師さんのところに行こう？」
lines.english: “O-oh, I know. Um, big brother... why don’t we go see the pastor?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえええ！　見るなっつってんだろおおお！」
lines.english: “Shut uuuuup! I said don't look at meeeeee!”

lines.japanese: 「せっ、世界が平和でありますようにっ」
lines.english: “May peace prevail on Earth!”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 声が届いた。
lines.english: The voice reached me.

lines.japanese: 懐かしい声だった。
lines.english: It was a voice I knew from long ago.
“Wait...”
“Kobato...?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、お、お兄ちゃん……？」
lines.english: “Oh! B-big brother...?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……おれ、ポッポの兄ちゃんだ……」
lines.english: “Yeah... I'm Poppo's big brother...”

lines.japanese: 気が付けば故郷の町。１２月の白い空。大切な小鳩。
lines.english: And when I came to, there was my hometown. A white December sky. My precious Kobato.

lines.japanese: この素晴らしき世界。
lines.english: This wonderful world.

lines.japanese: 俺の自我がここにあった。
lines.english: My self was here.

lines.japanese: 「でも……だめだよ、おれ、ならくの刑だも……」
lines.english: “But... I can't. I got sentenced to the Abyss...”

lines.japanese: 「悪いことしたやつは、ばつをうけなきゃだめだも……もうこっちにはいらんないも……」
lines.english: “If you do something bad, you gotta be punished... I can't stay over here anymore...”

lines.japanese: 「い、いいのっ！　教会いっしょに行こっ。そこでゆっくり、いろんな話をすればいいから」
lines.english: “I-it's all right! Let's go to the church together. We can take our time and talk about everything there.”

lines.japanese: 嫌だった。もう何もかもが嫌だった。俺は子供のようにべそをかいて鼻をすすった。
lines.english: I didn't want to. I was sick of everything. I whimpered like a child and snuffled through my nose.

lines.japanese: 小鳩が俺を支えて歩きだす。俺は帰りたかったけど、でも抗えない。妹のそばにいてやらなきゃならない。彼女がそう望むなら、俺は十字架を折ってでも叶えてやる必要がある。
lines.english: Kobato supported me as we began to walk. I wanted to go home, but I couldn’t refuse her. I had to stay by my little sister’s side. If she wanted it, I had to grant it, even if it meant snapping a cross in two.

lines.japanese: だってそれは母の遺言だから。
lines.english: Because that was Mother's dying wish.

lines.japanese: 道程は覚えていないが、気付いたら狭苦しい住宅街の中に、想い出の教会がひっそり佇んでいた。
lines.english: I remembered nothing of the walk. When awareness returned, the church from my memories stood quietly amid a cramped residential neighborhood.

lines.japanese: 情けないことに、俺は妹の肩に体重の半ばを預けていた。脚の筋肉が弛緩しきっていて、どうしても踏んばってくれないんだ。
lines.english: Pathetically, I had put half my weight on my sister's shoulder. Every muscle in my legs had gone slack and simply refused to brace me.

lines.japanese: 「着いたね、お兄ちゃん」
lines.english: “We’re here, Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: 健気な声の中にかすかな息切れが混じっていた。
lines.english: A faint breathlessness mingled with her brave little voice.

lines.japanese: 「こんな小さかったっけ……」
lines.english: “Was it always this small...?”

lines.japanese: 冗談めかして笑うつもりだったのに、嫌みたらしいかすれ声が出てしまった。
lines.english: I had meant to make a joke of it and laugh, but what came out was a rasp edged with bitterness.

lines.japanese: 小鳩は曖昧に頷いた。
lines.english: Kobato gave a noncommittal nod.

lines.japanese: 妹に支えられた兄。傍から見たら、いまの俺たちはどんな風に映るんだろう。
lines.english: A brother supported by his little sister. What did we look like from the outside?

lines.japanese: 俺はいくら笑われてもいいけど、小鳩が笑われるようなことだけはしたくないと思った。
lines.english: I didn't care how much they laughed at me, but I never wanted to do anything that would make them laugh at Kobato too.

lines.japanese: 倒れこむように長椅子へ横たわった。
lines.english: I collapsed onto a pew.

lines.japanese: すぐ隣りにそっと腰を下ろす妹。ひんやりした手が額に触れた。
lines.english: My sister gently lowered herself beside me. A cool hand touched my brow.

lines.japanese: 静まりかえった礼拝堂に、みっともなく乱れた俺の息遣いが響いている。忘れたい過去が心臓に鞭を入れてるみたいだった。眠りたいのに全身の血液がぐつぐつ騒いでいた。
lines.english: My ragged, shameful breathing echoed through the deathly still chapel. The past I wanted to forget seemed to be whipping my heart. I wanted to sleep, but all the blood in my body boiled and clamored.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、ここにいると安心しない？」
lines.english: “Big Brother, doesn’t it feel safe in here?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……そうだね……」
lines.english: “Yes... I do...”

lines.japanese: 俺は寝そべったまま涙声で応えた。わけも分からず下顎が震えていた。
lines.english: Still flat on my back, I answered through tears. For some reason I could not understand, my jaw was trembling.

lines.japanese: 妹が気遣ってくれていた。上体だけでも起こしたいと思ったけど、無理だった。
lines.english: My sister was worried about me. I wanted to at least sit up, but I couldn't.

lines.japanese: 「だいじょうぶだよ」
lines.english: “It's all right.”

lines.japanese: 「だいじょうぶだから」
lines.english: “Everything will be all right.”

lines.japanese: 「あのとき私を守ってくれたおにいちゃんは、私のたったひとりのお兄ちゃん」
lines.english: “The brother who protected me that day is the only brother I'll ever have.”

lines.japanese: 「これからもずうっといっしょにいたい」
lines.english: “I want us to stay together forever and ever.”

lines.japanese: 「おにいちゃんが大好きだよ」
lines.english: “I love you, big brother.”

lines.japanese: 走ってきたわけでもないのにぜいぜいと喘いでいる俺の髪を、小鳩の手が優しく撫でつける。
lines.english: I hadn’t even been running, but I was gasping for breath. Kobato gently smoothed my hair.

lines.japanese: 「うん……俺もだ……」
lines.english: “Yes... I love you too...”

lines.japanese: 俺はその手を拾いあげて握った。
lines.english: I lifted that hand and held it.

lines.japanese: 「やっとお兄ちゃんといっしょになれたね」
lines.english: “At last, we’re together, big brother.”
